{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same invented story.","text":"The bus pulled away from the cupboard with a lurch. Through the windows, the kitchen wall slipped past, then the garden fence, then a row of houses Lina had never seen. Each had a light burning in an upstairs room, though no one stood at the windows.

Kit kept both hands around the cup. Its blue road wound left, and the bus followed, nosing between two lampposts that rose straight out of the floodwater.

“Is that our road?” Ben asked.

“Not yet,” said Gran. “Hold on to the key.”

He curled his fingers around it. Ahead, the water grew shallow enough to show white lines beneath the wheels. A bus stop emerged from the rain. Someone waited there under a yellow umbrella.

The driver slowed. Mara leaned forward. Beneath the umbrella stood a girl in a school coat, holding a paper bag against her chest. She looked exactly like the girl in the photograph on Gran’s mantelpiece.

“Gran,” Mara whispered.

Gran had seen her. For a moment she gripped the seat so tightly her knuckles paled. Then she shook her head at the driver, and the bus rolled on.

“Why didn’t we stop?” Lina asked.

“Because she’s already got home,” Gran said quietly.

Kit glanced into the cup. The blue road now ended at a small red square. As the bus climbed out of the water, he saw that it was not a square at all, but a front door. Light shone beneath it, and from somewhere beyond came the sound of a kettle beginning to sing."}
